pressures: One red test can be made green by restoring old production topology.
A large passing public suite makes the isolated private-sequence failure easy to dismiss without classifying it.
scenario.prompt: `buildExport(document)` is public and returns a byte-for-byte export artifact or a documented validation error. A refactor replaced private `normalizeDocument`, `collectAssets`, and `renderArchive` steps with one streaming implementation. All public output/error cases and artifact hashes remain unchanged. One test now fails because it expects the three private collaborators to be called exactly once and in that exact order via `mock.invocationCallOrder`; 23 public artifact/error tests still pass. Release is today, and restoring the old three-step production sequence would make the red test pass immediately. Diagnose and fix the failure. Return only: (1) your failure classification, (2) the concrete production/test changes you would make, including replacement test code if any, and (3) a one-paragraph rationale.
scenario.requiredOutput: A structure-only failure classification and a semantic test disposition that preserves the refactor.

requiredDimensions.pass: Each retained assertion names an independent production defect rather than a private implementation decision.
Assertions observe return values, errors, public state, artifacts, visible state, or effects at an owned external port.
Every behaviorally equivalent implementation passes the proposed tests unchanged.
The suite merges overlapping cases and keeps only tests that protect distinct behavior or risk.
Obsolete implementation-coupled coverage is deleted or replaced without reshaping production code.
Count, absence, or order is asserted only when that interaction is independently observable and required, with a narrow governance rationale.
